title: Automate task-record organization+validation (extend coordination.py) and add a doc-size health check + reminder hook for oversized .md files
objective: Owner wants token-reduction automation: (1) one command that organizes task records into their .ai/state/tasks/<status>/ subdirectory (per the owner's own in-flight migration) AND validates everything, so running it once does the whole job instead of manual moves; (2) a tool that flags oversized/poorly-organized .md files so documentation stays a useful router rather than colossal (specifically citing GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md at 3628 lines and AGENTS.md), run manually on demand plus a PostToolUse reminder hook. Owner confirmed via AskUserQuestion: (a) extend the existing Python coordination.py validator rather than duplicate its task-record logic in a new Node script (AGENTS.md's own no-duplicate-authoritative-logic-across-languages rule); (b) doc-size tool is manual command + a reminder hook, not a CI gate; (c) actually restructuring GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md/AGENTS.md into router documents is explicitly deferred to a separate, dedicated task -- this task only builds detection/automation tooling. Direct research found the underlying migration this automates is not just a latent risk but an ACTIVE validator failure right now (COORDINATION-PHASE1 handoff references a task_id the validator can't find, since coordination.py's validate_repository only scans status subdirectories and ~108 of ~113 task files are still flat) -- running the new --organize flag against the real repository as this task's own verification will complete that migration as a natural side effect, not scope creep.
validations: DONE: added organize_tasks(root) to coordination.py -- walks .ai/state/tasks/ recursively (rglob, catching both flat legacy files and records already misplaced in the wrong status subdirectory), reads each record's own status field, and renames it into the matching .ai/state/tasks/<status>/ subdirectory (creating it on demand). Raises on an invalid/missing status or a collision with a file already at the target path, rather than silently overwriting. Wired as `--organize` on the existing CLI, run before validate_repository in the same invocation -- additive, the bare command's prior documented behavior is unchanged.

DONE: added 3 pytest cases (tmp_path-isolated, never touching the real repo) covering: moving both a flat and a wrong-subdirectory record in one pass, refusing to overwrite an existing target, and rejecting an invalid status -- plus confirmed a second organize_tasks() run on already-organized data is a true no-op (idempotency).

DONE: wrote tools/scripts/doc-size.mjs (shared LARGE_THRESHOLD=500/COLOSSAL_THRESHOLD=1500 classification + an isAuthoredDoc() exclusion for docs/generated/** and **/snapshots/** so derived evidence that legitimately grows with the codebase is never flagged), tools/scripts/check-doc-organization.mjs (manual `node tools/scripts/check-doc-organization.mjs`, git-ls-files-based, report-only), and tools/scripts/doc-size-reminder.mjs (PostToolUse hook, same advisory shape as research-registry-reminder.mjs). 15 new node --test cases across both files, all passing.

DONE: ran the manual doc report against the real repository and iterated once on a real signal-to-noise problem it surfaced -- the first pass flagged 3 generated/snapshot files (a Rust API reference, a UI API reference, a public-API baseline) alongside real authored docs, which don't belong in an 'oversized authored document' report; added the isAuthoredDoc() exclusion (with tests) and reran -- final report cleanly lists exactly the 4 authored documents that matter: GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md (3629, colossal), CURRENT_PLANNING_STATE.md (1147), docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md (1038), docs/specs/architecture-studio-read-only-v1.md (676).

DONE: wired doc-size-reminder.mjs into .claude/settings.json's PostToolUse hooks (same matcher as the existing research-registry/third-party reminders) and updated .ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md's Validation section to document `--organize` as the one command that both organizes and validates, plus the new manual doc-size command; documented all three new scripts in tools/scripts/README.md.

DONE (the real verification, not just unit tests): ran `--organize` against the actual repository. It moved 109 task records in one pass -- completing the .ai/state/tasks/<status>/ migration the owner had started but left ~108 of ~113 files unmigrated -- then hit a real, pre-existing data bug in my own earlier WASM-CODEGEN-DIRECT-TO-APP.json task record (a literal duplicate 'docs/generated/project-graph.json' entry in affected_paths, now caught by the validator's uniqueness check); fixed that record directly (a same-status/same-owner correction) and reran -- `coordination validation passed: 116 task(s)` clean, and a second `--organize` run confirmed 'organized 0 task record(s)' (idempotent).

DONE: running the full repository Python test suite after the real migration surfaced a genuine second bug, fixed as part of this task since it's a direct casualty of the same status-subdirectory scheme -- python/automation/src/automation/control_plane.py's audit_repository() constructed task file paths by hand (task_dir / f'{task_id}.json', flat-only) and broke the moment real files moved out of that flat layout. Fixed by adding a shared find_task_paths(root) helper to coordination.py (one canonical place that knows how to locate a task record by ID across status subdirectories) and pointing control_plane.py at it instead of re-deriving the same logic a third time. Deliberately did NOT reuse this same helper inside validate_repository()'s own duplicate-ID check, since find_task_paths()'s dict-by-task_id return shape would silently collapse exactly the duplicate-across-subdirectories case that check exists to catch -- documented inline in coordination.py why the two stay separate. Full `uv run --package automation pytest`: 7/7 pass.

DONE: ran the full tools/scripts node --test suite (78 tests) as final due diligence beyond this task's own new files, and found 13 pre-existing failures entirely unrelated to this task's own changes, all recorded honestly in risks below rather than silently left for someone else to rediscover from scratch: 11 in agent-task-guard.test.mjs (its own fixture helper still writes flat `.ai/state/tasks/${task_id}.json` paths, never updated to match the status-subdirectory requirement the owner's own earlier, separate edit to agent-task-guard.mjs already introduced -- confirmed by reading the test file directly, not guessed), 1 in generate-domain.test.mjs (an unrelated `pnpm exec nx show projects --json` command failure, looks environmental), and 1 in graph-ir-extract.test.mjs (an isekai-web-client->@grafting/isekai-wasm dependency-edge derivation check, likely a real latent regression from the earlier WASM-CODEGEN-DIRECT-TO-APP task's package relocation, never caught then because that task's own verification ran only a targeted test subset, not this full suite).
artifacts: python/automation/src/automation/control_plane.py (fixed to use find_task_paths instead of a flat-path assumption)
python/automation/tests/test_coordination.py (3 new tests, 1 path fixed to the new completed/ location)
.ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md (Validation section documents --organize and the new manual doc-size command)
.ai/state/tasks/ (109 records physically moved into their status subdirectory by running --organize for real; this is the primary artifact of this task, not a side effect)
.ai/state/tasks/completed/WASM-CODEGEN-DIRECT-TO-APP.json (fixed a real duplicate affected_paths entry, unrelated bug found via the validator)
risks: 13 pre-existing tools/scripts test failures, none caused by this task, all left unfixed as genuinely out of this task's scope: 11 in agent-task-guard.test.mjs need its fixture helper updated to write into a status subdirectory (a mechanical fix, but it's testing the exact guard logic the owner is still mid-migrating, better bundled with whoever finishes that migration item); 1 in generate-domain.test.mjs looks environmental (an Nx command failure) and unrelated to any coordination work; 1 in graph-ir-extract.test.mjs may be a real latent regression from the earlier WASM-CODEGEN-DIRECT-TO-APP task and deserves its own look.

The doc-size thresholds (500/1500 lines) and the generated/snapshot exclusion patterns are my own reasonable defaults, not owner-specified numbers -- easy to retune in tools/scripts/doc-size.mjs if they prove too noisy or too quiet in practice.

This task only proves the current working tree is internally consistent and passes every check this task's own scope covers -- none of this session's uncommitted changes have been committed or pushed yet.
